solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: An aquatic bird to avoid? (4)

blocks.note: a common water bird of ponds and rivers
the verb for dodging a blow or a question by bobbing down

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher's riddle about which water bird to steer clear of.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that the two halves are separate meanings of one word rather than a bird you should dodge.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun is the plain bird name; the verb, to bob down out of the way, extends to dodging anything unwelcome.

entries.clue: No longer employed, treated with contempt around university (7)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means encircling, so the letters for 'treated with contempt' are wrapped about the U

annotation.surface: A sacked academic sneered at on campus.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a laid-off worker scorned at university; the definition describes a thing that has fallen out of use.
annotation.definitionFit: Employed here means used rather than hired, so a tool no longer employed is out of use.

entries.clue: OK, nonsense writer taking husband’s place in gamble (9)

indicatorNotes.taking: 'taking' someone's place means replacing them, so the writer stands in for the husband
indicatorNotes.place in: 'place in' names the slot inside the gamble word where the husband letter stood

blocks.note: H = husband, the letter swapped out
Edward Lear, author of nonsense verse, the letters swapped in

annotation.surface: A nonsense poet stepping into a husband's role in a wager, and it's all approved.
annotation.walkthrough: Edward Lear wrote The Owl and the Pussy-cat and popularised the limerick, which makes him the crossword's standard nonsense writer.
annotation.definitionFit: The noun OK, as in 'got the OK', is official permission, which is what clearance means.

entries.clue: Brotherhood stumbled over women’s transport (10)

annotation.surface: Monks tripping over the women's carriage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' is a preposition in the surface but gives O, the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over of six balls.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both words name a company of people bound by shared interest or friendship.

entries.clue: Short of energy, they are terribly coarse (6)

indicatorNotes.Short of: being short of something means lacking it, so the energy letter goes missing
indicatorNotes.terribly: 'terribly' says the letters are in a terrible state, jumbled out of order

annotation.surface: A complaint that some lethargic people are terribly rude.
annotation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Es goes; the six letters left are then rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is crude and unrefined, the sense of coarse that applies to manners and jokes.

entries.clue: Raised in social status, reorganising field day (8)

indicatorNotes.reorganising: the letters of FIELD DAY are rearranged

annotation.surface: A social climber organising a village field day.
annotation.walkthrough: A rare word, so the anagram fodder beside the indicator is the way in.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare word built from lady plus -fy, meaning made into a lady, that is, lifted to genteel rank.

entries.clue: London feature later represented in court game? (8,6)

indicatorNotes.represented: LATER is presented again in a new order
indicatorNotes.in: the rearranged letters go into WOO

annotation.surface: A London landmark that later turns up as part of a tennis or squash game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court game' looks like one sport, tennis or squash, but splits into a verb and a card game. The bridge itself crosses the Thames in central London.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the bridge is one of the landmark crossings of the Thames.

entries.clue: Israeli port’s condition, enveloped in a lot of sea mist (5)

indicatorNotes.enveloped in: IF is wrapped inside the mist
indicatorNotes.a lot of: most, not all, of HAAR is used

blocks.note: HAAR, a cold sea fog on the east coast of Britain, minus its last letter
if = on condition that; IF goes inside

annotation.surface: A report on the weather at an Israeli harbour shrouded in fog.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay. Haar is a word for the sea fret that rolls in off the North Sea.
annotation.definitionFit: Haifa is Israel's major northern seaport.

entries.clue: Gemstone European delivered in ceramic vessel (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'delivered in' reads as placed inside, so the European and delivered letters sit within the vessel

blocks.note: delivered = rid, freed (as in delivered from evil)

annotation.surface: A jewel from Europe arriving packed in a clay pot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' suggests a parcel, but here it means set free, as in 'deliver us from evil'.
annotation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a gem-quality olivine.

entries.clue: Military award belonging to woman inferior to many? (6,2,6)

indicatorNotes.inferior to: in a down clue, OF HONOUR sits below LEGION

blocks.note: legion = many, as in 'their number is legion'
Honour is a woman's first name

annotation.surface: A medal owned by a lady who is outranked by the crowd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inferior' means lower down: in a down entry OF HONOUR is placed beneath LEGION.
annotation.definitionFit: The Legion of Honour is France's highest order of merit, awarded for military and civil service.

entries.clue: Plantigrade mammal southern ambassador put up with (3-4)

blocks.note: HE = His Excellency, an ambassador's title
to bear = to put up with

annotation.surface: A diplomat from the south has to tolerate a flat-footed beast.
annotation.walkthrough: An ambassador is addressed as His Excellency. Plantigrade animals walk on the soles of their feet, as bears do.
annotation.definitionFit: A she-bear is a female bear, and bears are plantigrade mammals.

entries.clue: Make row outside back of market, getting more bananas (7)

indicatorNotes.outside: 'outside' means on the outer side, so the row word stands around the market letter

blocks.note: a tier is a row, split around T
last letter of market, inside TIER

annotation.surface: A stallholder arguing at the rear of the market over a bigger bunch of bananas.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests an argument but means a line, as of seats. Bananas is slang for crazy, so 'more bananas' is a comparative.
annotation.definitionFit: Slang synonyms: dotty and bananas both mean crazy, and both take the comparative here.

entries.clue: What a conscientious nurse makes on reaching hospital? Easy (15)

annotation.definition2: What a conscientious nurse makes on reaching hospital?

blocks.clueFragment: What a conscientious nurse makes on reaching hospital?
blocks.note: a cryptic description: where does a dutiful nurse head without dawdling?
a plain synonym for simple, uncomplicated

annotation.surface: A diligent nurse arriving for her shift, and it's no trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: The cryptic half splits the answer as STRAIGHT FOR WARD: a dutiful nurse makes straight for the ward.
annotation.definitionFit: A task with no twists or complications is easy; the other half reads the word as three.

entries.clue: Eating at home, with wild dog mostly around (6)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means surrounding, so the shortened dog wraps the at-home letters

blocks.note: DINGO, the Australian wild dog, without its last letter; split around IN

annotation.surface: Having a meal in the house while dingoes prowl nearby.
annotation.walkthrough: The insertion comes right after the first letter of the dog, which makes the answer look like a simple -ING word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dining is eating, usually a proper meal at table.

entries.clue: Begged to share the Scarlet Pimpernel’s fate? (8)

blocks.note: what happens to the hero of Baroness Orczy's novel, hunted everywhere

annotation.surface: Pleading not to end up hunted like the Scarlet Pimpernel.
annotation.walkthrough: The Scarlet Pimpernel's famous rhyme runs 'They seek him here, they seek him there', so his fate is to BE SOUGHT.
annotation.definitionFit: Beseech means to beg earnestly, and its past tense is used here; the second half splits it into two words.

entries.clue: A couple of chaps producing headgear in Scotland (9)

annotation.surface: Two men making hats north of the border.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'couple of chaps' are two first names side by side, which also happen to be Scottish place names.
annotation.definitionFit: A glengarry is a boat-shaped Scottish cap worn with Highland dress.

entries.clue: Work supported by sure winner in firm (8)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in firm' means held within the company, so the firm's letters go around the rest

blocks.note: CO = company, a firm; the outer shell
a cert is a racing certainty

annotation.surface: A job in a company backed by a safe bet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' reads as employment but means a musical composition.
annotation.definitionFit: A concerto is a musical work for soloist and orchestra.

entries.clue: Amphibian got turned over crossing bank by river (4,4)

indicatorNotes.turned over: something turned over is flipped end to end, so its letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.crossing: to cross something is to lie across it, so the reversed word straddles the bank and river
indicatorNotes.by: 'by' means next to, so the river letter is set beside the bank

blocks.note: GOT reversed, split around what follows
a reef is a bank of rock or sand

annotation.surface: A frog flipped over while hopping across a riverbank.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks like a riverbank but means a reef, a ridge in the water.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: tree frogs are the climbing members of the frog family.

entries.clue: Blunder involving swimmer in turbulent water (4-3)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve is literally to roll in, so the blunder word takes the fish inside it

blocks.note: a trip = a slip, blunder; split T…RIP
the ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: A swimmer's mistake while caught in rough water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person but is a fish, the IDE, a crossword regular.
annotation.definitionFit: A tide-rip is a stretch of rough, turbulent water where tides meet.

entries.clue: Superior nun given directions by a couple of bishops (6)

blocks.note: B = bishop in chess notation, twice

annotation.surface: A Mother Superior taking instructions from two bishops.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Given directions' sounds like being told what to do; here directions are compass points added after the bishops.
annotation.definitionFit: An abbess is the nun in charge of an abbey, a Mother Superior.

entries.clue: High-flyer from Kentucky with pounds in a Channel Island (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in a Channel Island' means located on the island, so its letters surround the state and pounds

blocks.note: Sark, one of the Channel Islands; the outer shell

annotation.surface: A wealthy American high-flyer bringing money to a tax haven island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High-flyer' suggests an ambitious person but is literal: the skylark sings high in the sky.
annotation.definitionFit: The skylark famously flies and sings very high up.

entries.clue: Downy plant Middle East scholar cut back (6)

indicatorNotes.cut back: the back, last letter, is cut off

blocks.note: ARABIST, an expert on the Arab world, minus its last letter T

annotation.surface: An Orientalist's garden plant being pruned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cut back' looks like a reversal instruction but only docks the tail.
annotation.definitionFit: Arabis, rock cress, is a plant with downy leaves.

entries.clue: Policeman’s lying about keeping agreement in an unnerving way (15)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means around in all directions, so the lying letters are thrown out of order
indicatorNotes.keeping: the outer pieces keep CONCERT inside

blocks.note: acting in concert = in agreement; kept inside

annotation.surface: A detective telling lies to cover up a deal, which is unsettling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lying' reads as dishonesty but supplies its own letters to be scrambled. The kept word sits between the policeman and the scramble.
annotation.definitionFit: Disconcertingly means in a way that unsettles or unnerves.

entries.clue: Function requiring weight and source of strength (5)

annotation.surface: A job description needing both heft and power.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Function' suggests a role or event; here it is the maths function.
annotation.definitionFit: Sinews, tendons and muscle, are the source of physical strength.

entries.clue: Animosity private soldier articulated (7)

indicatorNotes.articulated: the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

blocks.note: a ranker is a soldier serving in the ranks rather than an officer

annotation.surface: A private voicing his resentment.
annotation.walkthrough: The homophone works in British pronunciation, where the final R of both words is silent.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean lasting bitterness and ill will toward someone.

entries.clue: Implore gunners to accept other ranks, by God! (7)

indicatorNotes.to accept: to accept something is to take it in, so the other ranks go inside the begging and the gunners

blocks.note: OR = other ranks, soldiers not officers

annotation.surface: Pleading with the artillery to let the privates in, with an oath.
annotation.walkthrough: The insertion lands at the join between the two outer pieces, so it reads like a simple charade. Begorra is a stage-Irish oath.
annotation.definitionFit: Begorra is an Irish euphemism for 'by God!'.

entries.clue: A forceful person, might he entertain round America? (10)

indicatorNotes.entertain: to entertain guests is to have them in your house, so HE holds the round letter and America

blocks.note: HE as printed, the outer shell

annotation.surface: Wondering whether a dynamo of a man could host a tour of America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb of possibility but is the noun, power.
annotation.definitionFit: A powerhouse is a person of great energy and force.

entries.clue: Malaysian in Borneo, extremely doughty and keen at first (4)

indicatorNotes.at first: take the first letters of and keen

blocks.note: first and last letters of doughty

annotation.surface: Praise for a brave and eager Bornean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a joining word but supplies its own first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: The Dyaks are indigenous peoples of Borneo, part of which is Malaysian.
